  "command": "python3 << 'EOF'\nfrom PIL import Image, ImageDraw\nimport numpy as np\n\nimg = Image.open('/Users/carlosrestrepo/Desktop/ailabcreations-logo.png')\narr = np.array(img).copy()\n\n# Circle parameters (measured from image)\ncx, cy = 200, 200  # center\nr_outer = 198      # outer radius (edge of gold border)\nr_inner = 192      # inner radius (inside of gold border)\nbg_color = (26, 26, 26)         # dark background\ngold_color = (201, 168, 130)    # gold border\n\n# Strategy: for each pixel in the white area (y > 312), \n# determine if it's inside the circle and fill appropriately\nfor y in range(313, 400):\n    for x in range(0, 400):\n        dx = x - cx\n        dy = y - cy\n        dist = (dx**2 + dy**2) ** 0.5\n        if dist <= r_outer:\n            if dist >= r_inner:\n                arr[y, x] = gold_color\n            else:\n                arr[y, x] = bg_color\n\n# Also fix the transition at y=312 — check that row is clean\n# The border should smoothly complete\n\nresult = Image.fromarray(arr)\nresult.save('/Users/carlosrestrepo/Desktop/ailabcreations-logo-fixed.png')\nprint(\"Saved fixed logo\")\nEOF",
  "description": "Fix cropped logo by completing the bottom arc"
}

why does cowork reach limits faster tha code here in vs code

> AGENT

A few reasons:

1. **Cowork is conversational** — it carries the full chat history in context, which fills up fast with back-and-forth messages.

2. **Claude Code (VS Code) compacts automatically** — it summarizes older parts of the conversation to free up context, so it lasts longer.

3. **Cowork loads more tools by default** — Gmail, Calendar, Obsidian etc. all take up token space even when not used.

4. **You tend to do more back-and-forth in Cowork** — quick questions and replies add up faster than focused coding tasks.

**Bottom line:** Use Claude Code (here) for longer work sessions. Use Cowork for quick tasks or when you need Gmail/Calendar access.
